chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zurara who said:
The one who brings a sacrificial animal for an Umrah without performing Hajj, let him sacrifice it before he shaves his head.

key_terms.هَدْيٍ: Sacrificial animal brought by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: When should the sacrificial animal be slaughtered for an independent Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, clarifies the procedural order of expiation (kaffarah) for the Umrah al-Mufrada, emphasizing that the slaughter of the sacrificial animal must precede the cutting of hair (halq or qasr). This sequence is critical in Shia fiqh as it ensures the pilgrim remains in a state of Ihram obligations until the sacrifice is completed, distinguishing it from the Hajj ritual where the order may vary depending on the type of Hajj. The ruling underscores the importance of adhering to the specific legal sequence to validate the completion of the minor pilgrimage.
